author: Stevens
case: Center for National Security Studies v. U.S. Department of Justice
form: One signed opinion following full merits submission resolves the statutory category and residual-exemption questions and the two independent compilation-access claims. Seven Justices share the complete lead rationale, with two partial joins on independent access. Separate writings perform the distinct added-scheduling and statutory-dissent functions. These forms and governing propositions were fixed before counts; one eligible author can carry the whole lead.
fit: Fit governs. Stevens's Reporters Committee work identifies the government-conduct interest and the significance of compiled private information, both necessary to this remand's separate privacy analysis. His frozen statutory position also preserves supported common evidence and functional categories without converting them into a universal exemption. Souter is a strong alternative through the same Landano and Klamath commitments; Stevens can state the category and privacy distinctions equally faithfully and has the lower count. Breyer is another lower-count candidate, but Stevens's particular work on compiled identifying records gives him the more direct fit for the entire opinion. Stone-Zsela supports the shared rule, and his additional scheduling proposal is preserved separately; personal authorship offers no unique advantage in the agreed lead. No changed Associate commitment or expansion is needed.
